text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Farooq Leghari will preside over the second meeting of the Council for Defence and National Security on January 28 to discuss the accountability process and the holding of elections on February 3.
- At least 10 people were killed and five injured when a passenger bus and a van collided head-on 25 km from Rawalpindi.
- The caretaker government has finally decided to substantially cut the size of ministries, divisions and other government departments to eliminate unnecessary expenditure.
- The government has decided to merge the state-run National Investment Trust and Investment Corporation of Pakistan and then privatise the merged organisation, an official source said.

- The state's Privatisation Commission has received 16 pre-qualification bids for the sale of state-run Habib Credit and Exchange Bank, the investment wing of the state-run Habib Bank of Pakistan, an official said.
- The chairman of the private Muslim Commercial Bank said the government has postponed plans to sell its 24 percent stake in the bank till the stock market improves.

- As many as 48 industrial projects financed by the state-run Pakistan Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation have been put up for sale to new investors after their previous owners failed to clear their debts.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has asked banks and financial institutions to publish names of election candidates who have defaulted on loan repayments since December 1, 1996.
- S.C. Lubrifin of Romania has asked state-run National Refinery to supply 24,000 tonnes of base oil for processing into lubricants.
- Pakistani vegoil rates are likely to slip next week because of depressed prices abroad, dealers said.

- The National Finance Commission unanimously finalised its recommendations for the distribution of the national resources between the centre and the provinces according to which the under-developed provinces of Balochistan and North West Frontier Province will get extra funds to meet their deficits.
- Sugar prices surged by one rupee per kilo in the wholesale market although sugar from India has also arrived.
